It looks like you're dealing with a nasty clog. Because both sink basins are holding standing water in "193d094a-b7fd-421c-a23f-1679c9264867", we can immediately pinpoint the location of the problem. The blockage isn't in the immediate drains of either basin; it's further down the line past the point where the two pipes join together.

Looking at the plumbing under the sink in "b427758a-0ac4-49de-9c28-0cf0d7a460d6", the two drains meet at the sanitary tee just above the P-trap (the U-shaped bend). This means your clog is either sitting right inside that P-trap or further back into the wall.

Here is how to tackle it, but there is a major safety hazard to address first.

⚠️ Critical Safety Warning

I see a bottle of Great Value drain cleaner sitting on the counter. If you have already poured that into the standing water, the water in that sink and inside those pipes is highly caustic and can cause severe chemical burns to your skin and eyes. You must proceed with extreme caution. Do not use a plunger right now, as it could splash the chemical water back at your face.

How to Clear the Clog

If you're ready to get your hands dirty, taking the plumbing apart is a straightforward mechanical fix.

  1. Suit Up: Put on thick, chemical-resistant rubber gloves and safety goggles.
  2. Bail the Water: Do not disconnect the pipes with the sink full. Use a cup to bail the standing chemical water out of the sink basins and carefully dump it into a bucket to dispose of down a toilet. Get the sinks as empty as possible.
  3. Prep the Area: Place a bucket directly underneath the P-trap in the cabinet and have old towels ready. Even after bailing the sink, water will still be trapped in that U-bend.
  4. Remove the P-trap: Unscrew the two slip-joint nuts on either end of the P-trap (the U-shaped pipe). They are designed to be hand-tightened, but if they are stuck, use a pair of channel-lock pliers to gently loosen them.
  5. Clear the Trap: Once the nuts are loose, pull the P-trap straight down. Dump the contents into your bucket. If it's packed full of sludge or food debris, you've found your culprit. Clean it out thoroughly.
  6. Check the Wall Pipe: If the P-trap is clear, the clog is further back in the pipe leading into the wall. You will need a plumbing snake (auger) to reach it. If you don't have one on hand, you might be able to snag an auger from your dad's workshop before making a trip to the hardware store. Feed the snake into the wall pipe, crank it through the resistance, and pull the blockage out.
  7. Reassemble: Put the P-trap back in place, ensuring the plastic slip washers are seated correctly. Hand-tighten the nuts (do not over-tighten, or the plastic will crack). Run hot water to test for leaks and ensure it drains cleanly.

Did you already pour that drain cleaner down the drain, or are we just looking at standard backup water?

turns.response_html:
Okay, that tells us exactly where the problem is. If the P-trap is clear but the sink is still backing up, the blockage is lodged deeper down the line in the pipe that runs straight back into the wall.

Here is how to tackle this next phase if you want to clear it yourself:

  1. Catch the Water Again: Put your bucket back under the sink and remove the P-trap one more time. You'll also want to unscrew the horizontal pipe (the trap arm) that connects the P-trap to the wall to give yourself direct access to the wall drain.
  2. Deploy a Drain Snake: You will need a plumbing snake (a hand auger) for this part. Feed the metal cable directly into the wall pipe.
  3. Break the Clog: Keep pushing the cable in until you hit resistance. Tighten the lock on the auger handle and turn the crank clockwise while pushing forward. This will help the tip corkscrew into the clog to either break it up or snag it so you can pull it out.
  4. Reassemble and Flush: Once you've cleared the blockage, reassemble the pipes, hand-tighten the nuts, and run hot water for a few minutes to flush any remaining debris down the main line.

Because this blockage is deep within the wall plumbing of the apartment, this is usually the exact point where it makes sense to hand the headache off to property maintenance so they can auger the main line for you.
